1 8 7 7. Tim trite saying that misfortunes never come single, is as true in the history of nations as in the lives of individuals. The year that is rapidly drawing to a close is a fit illustration of this. It began with the news of a great calamity; it ends in gloom; its course has been that of misfortune and dietremi on every

side. Place ajar domes. Turning fleet to countries outside Great Britain. On New Year's day the country was startled with the news that a terrible hurricane, followed by • large tidal wave, had ravaged a populous district in India, and that nearly a quarter of a million of preppie had perished. This ill- news was afterwards modified, but though the mortality from the ffet shock was leas than it was eupposed to be, the death rate was greatly increased by the fever awl dyeentry which followed upon the flood. Unhappily it is impossible to guard against these destructive freaks of nature. During the summer, rumours came that famine was deeoleting a large section of the Mysore district. The rumours gave place to cer- tainty, and the awful fact became patent that mutt numbers of our fellow-subjects must inevitably perish. It took some time to rouse the public to a true sense of the calamity, but when once it was understood, the appeal to British generosity was mucosa- N. and in spite of bad trade nearly half a million of money was rained, and sent to India; one fifth of this sum having been contributed by Lancashire. Meanwhie the Indian Government worked with commend- able zeal and wisdom, and everything was done that human agency °odd aueunlplisn to mitigate the Buffering. It is to be hoped that the warning wilt not be in vela bat that the peo;ile at home will take a more intelligent in-errs in the good governmt n and welfare of their 200,000,000 fellow sub jade in the Bast then they nave hitherto done. Famine has also visited China, but owing to the difficulty of procuring authentic news the extent is not known. The plague broke out at Baghdad, but happily did not spread. America has suffered very ly from bail trade, which has been aggravated by the strike of railway servants at an eatimated loss of eight millions sterling, and by the whole/ode defalcations and swindling in some of the large cities. In Jlaroh Mr. II eyes was declared to have been elected President of the Union. Re hae adopted a wise policy of conciliation to the r oath, and has shewn • (Reim to purge the civil service of its corruption and jobbery, and has given evidence of • desire to reduce the duties on imports, and to resort to the honest course of paying the national debt in gold and not in silver or greenbacks. C ,nada has been blessed with a bountiful harvest, which has been suilloient to arrest the great demerit on ot her commerce. New Brunswick has had to witness the destruction of one third of her beautiful capital by tire. In South Africa one of our "little were" was happily WTI eoncluded. The meet notable events in that splendid continent have been the unification of the new states by the South African 11,11 ; and the tracing of the Congo river by Mr. Stanley. wester. Europe, although kept in sus- penile by the war, has enj yed freedom from ec'ual strife. France has peened safely through a great crisis ; and one of the turn- ing points in her history has been mimes. fully rounded, thanks to the Fatima for- bearance of the Republican& The President has been around of yielding to the pc enure of royalist or imperialist partizan., and of submitting to the dictation of priestly coun- sellors. At one time he appeared to be struck with a judicial blindness that would lead to his own destruction or hie country's ruin. Happily the difference is composed France resumes her true position as a great power ; and la at rest to pursue her peaceful avocations. Germany, Austria, and Italy, are watching the result in the.Eaet, and are also watching one another. The opening year found the accredited ambassadors still in conference at Con- . stantinople, and on the lath Jan. the final propoea/s of the conference to the Porte were adopted. They were rejected. and negocia- , lions ended on the twentieth. On the 24th April Russia declared war with Turkey, and three days later the first engagement between the contending armies took place.
